newsitem.title: USA: Most NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, longs exit late.
newsitem.headline: Most NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, longs exit late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended steady to lower Friday in a sluggish session, with a late wave of long liquidation before the weekend driving front months into negative territory, sources said.

August slipped 2.1 cents to close at $2.094 per million British thermal units after climbing early to $2.14. September settled two cents lower at $2.104. Other deferreds ended unchanged to down 1.4 cents.
"We saw some long liquidation before the weekend but it was pretty quiet," said one East Coast trader, noting August closed well within its recent technical range.

Chart traders pegged August support at this week's low of $2.051, with resistance first seen at $2.15. Major selling was expected along the down trendline at $2.24, with psychological buying likely at $2.
Traders said forecasts for warm Northeast and Midwest temperatures into early next week helped lift paper early.
But with more seasonal weather expected later in the week, few predicted a major break to the upside.
They said continued heat in Texas and the Southwest next week may be enough to hold prices in current ranges.

In the cash Friday, weekend Gulf Coast prices edged up one cent to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also was modestly higher near the $2.40 level.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell one cent to $2.192. NYMEX said 21,437 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 23,495.

On the KCBT, August finished 1.3 cents lower at $1.992, while deferreds ended down by one to two cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 10.2 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 178 lots traded, up from Thursday's total of 107.
